chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from Humran ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed Jibra'il عليه السلام came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله with two pomegranates. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ate one of them, and he broke the other into two halves. He ate one half and fed Ali half. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “O my brother, do you know what these two pomegranates are?” He said: “No.” He said: “As for the first, it is prophethood; you have no share in it. And as for the other, it is knowledge; you are my partner in it.”

So I said: “May Allah keep you well, how was he his partner in it?” He said: “Allah did not teach Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله any knowledge except that He commanded him to teach it to Ali عليه السلام.”

key_terms.الرُّمَّانَتَانِ: the two pomegranates, symbolic of prophethood and knowledge
key_terms.النُّبُوَّةُ: prophethood, a station specifically denied here to Imam Ali عليه السلام
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: divinely taught knowledge shared with Imam Ali عليه السلام
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلَ: Jibra'il عليه السلام, the angelic messenger who brought the symbolic gift
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, recipient of revelation and divine knowledge
key_terms.شَرِيكِي: my partner, indicating participation in the Prophet’s knowledge
key_terms.عَلِيًّا: Imam Ali عليه السلام, designated as the Prophet’s partner in knowledge

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Imam Ali’s partnership with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله in knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Jibra'il عليه السلام brought two pomegranates to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, one symbolizing prophethood and the other knowledge. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله clarified that Imam Ali عليه السلام had no share in prophethood, but was his partner in knowledge, and that every knowledge taught to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was also commanded to be taught to Ali عليه السلام. The narration highlights the unique rank of Imam Ali عليه السلام in receiving the prophetic inheritance of divinely taught knowledge.
